results.question: Can I upload FERPA-protected student data to Claude at Syracuse?
results.answer:
**Yes — when logged in with your SU NetID, you may use Claude with FERPA-protected student data at Syracuse University.**

Here are the key details:

## ✅ FERPA Data is Permitted with NetID Login

Claude Enterprise explicitly states that **all Data Classification Definitions of university data** (which includes FERPA-protected data) may be used when you are logged in with your Syracuse University credentials (NetID) at [getclaude.syr.edu](https://getclaude.syr.edu) [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].

## 🔒 Key Data Protections in Place

- **No model training:** Data you upload and your chats are **not** used to train Claude's AI models by default. The only exception is if you explicitly submit feedback or a bug report [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].
- **You own your data:** You retain ownership of your inputs, and are granted ownership of outputs Claude creates [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].
- **No unauthorized external transmission:** When Claude executes code (bash, Python, R), network access is disabled to prevent university data from being sent to external endpoints [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].
- **IT access governance:** Data is accessible to authorized SU IT staff only for support, security, and maintenance purposes, governed by the IT Resources Acceptable Use policy [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].

## ⚠️ Important Caution

- **Retention:** All data is retained on the platform for **2 years**, even items you delete (they remain on the platform even if no longer visible to you) [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].
- **Shared artifacts:** Be careful about sharing Claude Projects or Artifacts — data included in shared items could be exposed to others [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].
- **Incognito/private chats:** Even in Incognito mode (not saved to chat history), data is still retained on the platform per the standard 2-year retention policy [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].

In short: Claude Enterprise via your SU NetID is an approved, protected environment for FERPA data — but exercise care around sharing and understand that retention persists even after deletion.

- Conversations are stored in your **M365 mailbox** and recoverable for up to 30 days after deletion [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]]

### 📊 Quick Policy Comparison

results.question: How do I install Claude Code on Windows?
results.answer:
Here is a step-by-step guide to installing Claude Code on Windows:

---

## Installing Claude Code on Windows

### Step 1: Get Access to Claude Code
Before installing, you need to have Claude Code access provisioned through Syracuse University. (See the Purchase Claude Code and Claude API Access page for details on obtaining access.)

---

### Step 2: Set the PowerShell Execution Policy
Open PowerShell and run the following command to allow local scripts to execute:
```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser
```

---

### Step 3: Download & Run the Install Script
An automated PowerShell script (`Install-DevTools.ps1`) handles the entire installation. It is available on the Claude Code Setup page and auto-detects your system architecture (AMD64 or ARM64).

**What gets installed:**

| Tool | Version | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Node.js | 24.12.0 | Portable/embedded |
| Git Portable | 2.52.0 | Includes Git Bash |
| Python Embeddable | 3.14.3 | Skipped if system Python detected |
| VS Code Portable | Latest | Skipped if already installed |
| GitHub Desktop | Latest | Visual interface for Git |
| PowerShell 7 | Latest | Installed via winget |
| Claude Code | Latest | Always installs locally |

By default, tools install to your **OneDrive** folder for sync across devices. Claude Code itself always installs locally to `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`.

---

### Step 4: Remove the "Mark of the Web"
Windows blocks scripts downloaded from the internet. You must unblock the file first:

- **Option 1 (Recommended):** Run in PowerShell:
  ```powershell
  Unblock-File -Path "$HOME\Downloads\Install-DevTools.ps1"
  ```
- **Option 2:** Right-click the file → Properties → check **Unblock** → click OK.

Then run the script:
```powershell
.\Install-DevTools.ps1
```

---

### Step 5: Configure Claude Code
1. Open a terminal and type `claude` to launch it.
2. Choose your preferred text display style.
3. Select **"Anthropic Console account"** (option 2) when prompted for login.
4. A browser window will open — sign in with your **`netid@syr.edu`** credentials. If prompted, select the **Syracuse University** organization.
5. Authorize Claude Code in the browser.
6. Return to the terminal and press **Enter twice** to accept and trust the folder.

✅ **You're all set!**

---

### Troubleshooting Tips
- If the script is still blocked, you can bypass the policy for a single session:
  ```powershell
  Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process
  ```
  Or from Command Prompt:
  ```
  powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\Install-DevTools.ps1
  ```
- **32-bit systems are not supported** — only AMD64 and ARM64.
- If OneDrive is unavailable, use the `-Location Local` flag when running the script.
- Verify internet connectivity, as some networks may block downloads [[986841103]].

---

**Sources:**
- [Claude Code Setup](https://answers.atlassian.syr.edu/wiki/spaces/ITSAI/pages/986841103/Claude+Code+Setup) [[986841103]]

results.answer:
Great — I now have everything I need from the hub and both raw pages. Here's a comprehensive answer:

---

# MCP (Model Context Protocol) at Syracuse University

## What Is MCP?

**MCP (Model Context Protocol)** is an open-source standard developed by Anthropic that allows Claude to securely connect to, read, and interact with external data sources and tools — such as files, folders, databases, APIs, and third-party SaaS platforms — directly from Claude [[claude-at-syracuse-product-surface-map]]. In plain terms, it's the technology that lets Claude "plug in" to other systems you use at work.

At SU, MCP shows up in two distinct forms: **Enterprise Connectors** (managed by ITS) and **Local MCP** (configured by individual users).

---

## Path 1: Enterprise Connectors (ITS-Managed)

These are MCP integrations enabled at the organizational level by ITS. Once ITS enables them, individual users can connect their personal accounts and toggle them on/off in Claude settings.

### ✅ Already Enabled for All SU Users

| Connector | What It Gives Claude Access To |
|---|---|
| **Microsoft 365** | SharePoint files, OneDrive documents, Teams messages, Outlook emails [[544210961]] |
| **Atlassian** | Jira tickets and Confluence pages [[841875458]] |

**How to activate M365:** Go to Claude Settings → Connectors → Microsoft 365 → Connect, and sign in with your `netid@syr.edu` account [[claude-at-syracuse-product-surface-map]].

### 🔒 Requesting a New Enterprise Connector

If you want a different third-party tool connected, you must submit a request to ITS — connectors cannot be self-enabled at the org level [[841875458]].

**Submit to:** [aihelp@syr.edu](mailto:aihelp@syr.edu) with:
1. The connector name and a link to vendor documentation
2. Your business use case
3. Confirmation of an SU vendor contract (if applicable)
4. A **SOC 2 Type II** report from the vendor *(the most critical requirement)*

**What ITS reviews:**
- SOC 2 Type II availability (requests go on hold without this)
- Whether SU already has a contract with the vendor
- Data classification risk (FERPA, HIPAA, PII, financial data face a higher bar)
- How broadly useful the connector is campus-wide
- Vendor/implementation maturity

**What will prevent approval:** No SOC 2 report, no SU contract, tool not approved for university data, or restricted data exposure without adequate controls [[841875458]].

---

## Path 2: Local MCP (User-Configurable, No ITS Approval Needed)

Local MCP runs entirely on your own machine without transmitting data to a third-party server, so it doesn't need enterprise admin approval [[841875458]]. You configure it yourself in **Claude Desktop**.

### Example: Connecting Claude Desktop to Power BI

Here's the step-by-step process documented for SU [[837517313]]:

1. **Install the extension:** Search for "Power BI Modeling MCP" in VS Code and install the one published by Microsoft.
2. **Find the `.exe` file:** Navigate to a path like:
   ```
   C:\Users\<YourUsername>\.vscode\extensions\analysis-services.powerbi-modeling-mcp-0.1.9-win32-x64\server
   ```
3. **Copy the path:** Hold Shift, right-click the `.exe`, and select "Copy as path."
4. **Open Claude Desktop config:** Click the "Edit config" button in the Claude Desktop app.
5. **Edit the config file** in VS Code and paste in:
   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "powerbi-modeling-mcp": {
         "command": "paste the path you copied here",
         "args": ["--start"],
         "env": {}
       }
     }
   }
   ```
   > ⚠️ Use **double backslashes** (`\\`) instead of single ones (`\`) in the path.
6. **Reboot** your computer and reopen Claude Desktop — you'll see the MCP listed.
7. **Use it:** Open a Power BI report, then in Claude Desktop type: *"Connect to the open Power BI desktop file"* and Claude will begin assisting with modeling tasks.

results.question: How does mentorAI differ from regular Claude.ai?

Here's a comprehensive comparison of **mentorAI** and **regular Claude.ai** at Syracuse University:

---

## mentorAI vs. Claude.ai at Syracuse University

### 🎯 Purpose & Design
- **Claude.ai** is a general-purpose AI assistant — a flexible tool for writing, research, coding, analysis, and more. It's a broad-purpose platform [[488210484]].
- **mentorAI** is a specialized platform built for **personalized, education-focused AI assistants**. It enables the creation of custom AI "mentors" grounded in specific course materials, textbooks, and faculty-approved content [[544505857]].

### 👤 Who It's For
- **Claude.ai** is for faculty, staff, and students who need a general AI tool for day-to-day tasks [[488210484]].
- **mentorAI** is purpose-built for the academic experience:
  - **Students** can build study mentors tailored to their courses, get adaptive feedback, and receive answers grounded in course materials with transparent citations [[544505857]].
  - **Faculty** can create course-specific AI teaching assistants to handle repetitive questions, assist with assignment feedback, and generate lesson plans — using only faculty-approved content [[544505857]].

### 📚 Knowledge Grounding
- **Claude.ai** answers from its general training data and any files/context you provide in the conversation.
- **mentorAI** grounds every answer in **verified, uploaded course materials** — not general knowledge — ensuring accuracy and academic integrity [[544505857]].

### 📊 Usage Limits
- **Claude.ai** has usage limits that vary by tier (standard vs. premium seat). Limits reset through the day but can be exhausted, especially with heavier models like Opus [[488210484]].
- **mentorAI** has **higher usage limits** than Claude.ai and may offer additional tools like **screen sharing** that Claude.ai does not [[488210484]]. In fact, the Claude FAQ explicitly recommends mentorAI as an alternative for users who anticipate hitting Claude's usage limits and don't want to pay for a premium seat.

### 🔧 Features
- **Claude.ai** offers multiple model tiers (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus), Projects, Artifacts, file uploads, M365 integrations, and code execution (with network access disabled for security) [[488210484]].
- **mentorAI** offers custom mentor creation, adaptive learning paths, assignment review assistance, curriculum design support, a web crawler, and an API — all within a platform run directly by Syracuse University [[544505857]].

### 🏛️ Platform Ownership
- **Claude.ai** is an Anthropic product that Syracuse University licenses through an Enterprise agreement [[488210484]].
- **mentorAI** is a **Syracuse University–run platform** (available at [mentor.ai.syr.edu](https://mentor.ai.syr.edu)), though it does incorporate Claude/Anthropic models under the hood [[544505857]].

---

**In short:** Claude.ai is the go-to general-purpose AI assistant, while mentorAI is a specialized, SU-operated platform focused on teaching and learning — with higher usage limits, course-specific knowledge grounding, and tools designed for the classroom.

results.question: What is MCP?
results.answer:
## What is MCP?

**MCP** stands for **Model Context Protocol** — an open-source standard developed by Anthropic that allows Claude to securely connect to, read from, and interact with external tools, systems, and data sources [[837517313]].

In practice, MCP is what powers **Claude Connectors** — integrations that extend Claude's capabilities beyond simple chat by giving it access to external systems like Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Jira, Confluence, Power BI, and more [[841875458]].

---

### Two Flavors of MCP at Syracuse University

1. **Enterprise Connectors (Cloud MCP)**
   These are configured at the organization level by ITS and allow Claude Enterprise to connect to third-party tools university-wide. Some connectors (like Microsoft 365 and Atlassian) are already enabled for all SU users. Others require a formal review and approval process before ITS can enable them [[841875458]].

2. **Local MCP (Claude Desktop)**
   This allows the Claude Desktop app to connect to data and tools *directly on your local computer* — such as local files, folders, databases, and APIs — without transmitting data to a third-party server. For example, it can connect Claude Desktop to Power BI reports running on your machine [[837517313]].

---

### Key Things to Know

- **Requesting a new connector:** Submit a request to [aihelp@syr.edu](mailto:aihelp@syr.edu) with the connector name, your business use case, confirmation of an SU vendor contract (if applicable), and a SOC 2 Type II report from the vendor [[841875458]].
- **Security review:** ITS evaluates connectors based on security compliance (SOC 2 Type II), data classification risk, existing university relationships with the vendor, and breadth of campus use [[841875458]].
- **You're in control:** When using local MCP, you control how much access Claude is granted to your local tools and data [[837517313]].

---

Available in the Claude Desktop app, this connector lets Claude **read, find, edit, and create files** in directories you explicitly grant access to. Local MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets Claude Desktop connect to **local data, files, databases, and apps running on your own computer** — without requiring enterprise admin approval. ## Approved SU AI Tools That Support File Uploads

Claude explicitly supports file uploads within conversations. The FAQ references file uploads multiple times — for example, noting that Claude's code execution environment "has access to any data you bring into your conversation — **whether through file uploads** or connected services like Microsoft 365" [[488210484]]. ### ✅ 2. Google Gemini (login as `NetID@g.syr.edu`)
Gemini explicitly supports file uploads. The FAQ states that prompts, chats, and **uploaded content** are not used to train Google's AI models, and that Gemini can only interact with "files you explicitly open, reference, or **share within a session**" [[498597967]]. This confirms you can bring files into a Gemini conversation. All SU data classifications are permitted when signed in with your SU Google account.

Copilot's FAQ references "**content** and prompts" and is built into Microsoft 365 apps (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, Outlook), meaning it can work with documents and files you have open or reference in those apps [[522289260]]. Claude helps write professional emails in an "Artifact" panel, covering:

- Internship follow-ups

Users refine drafts with iterative prompts ("Make this more formal", "Shorten to 120 words"). Claude does **not** integrate directly with Gmail or Outlook — you copy and paste the final draft.

- **Article summarization** (bullet-point format)
- **Multi-source comparison** (up to 5 documents at once, synthesis matrices)
- **Literature review outlines** organized by theme

- **Web search** for current research

- **Artifacts** as editable, living documents (outlines, bibliographies)

---

## 🔵 Gemini — Example Use Cases (1 topic)

### 1. Smart Study Companion [[515801118]]
Gemini's featured use case is building a personalized "Tutor Gem" — a custom AI helper configured with your own instructions and uploaded course materials. Key capabilities:
- **Multiple-choice quiz generation** from notes (with answers and explanations)
- **Article summarization** into 3 main points with an "Overall Insight" section
- **Step-by-step formula explanations** in a tutoring style, including common mistakes

A major differentiator: Gems can be **shared** with classmates via a link (e.g., through Blackboard or Google Classroom). Sharing exposes only the Gem's structure — not your uploaded files or chat history.

| Feature | Claude | Gemini |
|---|---|---|
| **Number of documented use cases** | 5 | 1 |
| **Study/learning support** | ✅ Study Project (flashcards, quizzes, summaries) | ✅ Tutor Gem (quizzes, flashcards, formula explanations) |

| **Custom persona/instructions** | ✅ Projects with persistent context | ✅ Gems with named instructions |
| **Web search** | ✅ | Not documented |
| **Google Drive/Classroom integration** | ❌ Not documented | ✅ (Gems can be shared via Classroom) |

---

## Key Takeaway
Claude has a much wider and more deeply documented set of example use cases — spanning professional workflows (emails, meetings, research) as well as academic support. Gemini's documented example focuses exclusively on **studying**, but goes into considerable depth on the Gem customization and sharing model, which is unique to Gemini's ecosystem. ## SU's Stance on AI Tools & Sensitive Data

### ✅ The Core Rule: Use Approved Tools + Your NetID

SU's position is that **all university data classifications — including confidential and restricted data — may be used with approved AI tools, provided you are logged in with your SU NetID credentials** [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]]. Using a personal account (e.g., a free Claude.ai or personal Gmail account) is NOT covered by university protections.

The officially approved tools are:
- **Anthropic Claude Enterprise** (getclaude.syr.edu)
- **mentorAI / Clementine Platform** (mentor.ai.syr.edu)
- **Microsoft Copilot** (Work or Web, via M365)
- **Google Gemini** (login with `NetID@g.syr.edu`)
- **Blackboard's AI**, **OpenAI ChatGPT Teams**, **Adobe Firefly**, **Gradescope**

---

### 🔒 Key Data Protection Guarantees (Per Tool)

| Protection | Claude Enterprise | Microsoft Copilot | Google Gemini |
|---|---|---|---|
| **No model training on your data** | ✅ Not used by default | ✅ Microsoft does not train on SU data | ✅ Not used to train Google's AI |
| **You own your inputs & outputs** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| **Data retention** | 2 years | Up to 30 days recoverable in M365 mailbox | Not specified |
| **Human review by vendor** | Not specified | Not specified | ✅ No human review by Google |

[[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]]

---

### ⚠️ Important Caveats

1. **IT Staff Access**: For Claude, Copilot, and Gemini alike, data is accessible to **authorized SU IT staff** for support, security, and maintenance purposes — governed by the IT Resources Acceptable Use Policy and Information Security Framework [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].

2. **Shared Artifacts**: Even within approved tools, be careful about data included in shared Claude Projects or Artifacts — sharing those could expose sensitive content [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].

3. **Incognito/Temporary Modes Don't Erase Data**: Claude's Incognito and Copilot's Temporary Chat modes simply hide chats from your history — data is **still retained on the platform** under standard policies [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].

4. **Claude Code Execution**: When Claude runs code (bash, Python, R), network access is disabled to prevent university data from being transmitted to external endpoints [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].

5. **Gemini Drive Access**: Gemini does **not** have unrestricted access to your entire Google Drive — only files you explicitly open or share in a session [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].

---

### ❌ What to Avoid

Do **not** use personal/consumer AI accounts (non-NetID logins) with university data. Only the approved tools accessed through SU credentials carry the institutional data protections described above [[approved-ai-tools-for-university-data]].

results.question: I'm trying to set up Claude on my Windows laptop for my research work and I need to know all the steps including how to get access, install the developer tooling, configure my SU account, and verify that I can use it day-to-day — what do I need to do, end to end?
results.answer:
Here is a complete end-to-end guide for setting up Claude on your Windows laptop for research at Syracuse University:

---

# 🎓 Claude Setup on Windows — End-to-End Guide for SU Researchers

---

## Phase 1: Get Access to Claude Enterprise (Chat)

**Step 1.1 — Sign up for your free SU Claude Enterprise account**

All SU faculty, staff, and students are entitled to a standard Claude Enterprise seat at no personal cost. Go to **[getclaude.syr.edu](https://getclaude.syr.edu)** and sign in with your `netid@syr.edu` credentials [[534642749]].

This gives you access to the Claude web chat interface (claude.ai) under SU's Enterprise agreement — which means:

- ✅ Your data is **not used to train** AI models (unless you explicitly submit feedback/bug reports) [[488210484]]
- ✅ You **retain ownership** of all inputs and outputs [[488210484]]
- ✅ You can upload **all SU data classifications** (including sensitive data) when logged in with your NetID [[488210484]]
- ✅ Chats are retained for **2 years** on the platform [[488210484]]

---

## Phase 2: Purchase Claude Code Access (for Developer Tooling)

The standard Enterprise license does **not** include Claude Code or API access — these are add-ons that require payment [[488210484]]. Your path depends on your role:

### If you are Faculty or Staff:
You have two options:

**Option A — Departmental Funds (recommended for ongoing use):**
Fill out the [Claude Code API Interest and Access Request Form](https://support.atlassian.syr.edu/servicedesk/customer/portal/791/group/1727/create/3601). You'll need to provide:
- A monthly spending cap (up to $200/month max via this route)
- A Fund 11 chart-string
- Your department's financial approver email
- Your IT lead email

Once processed, you'll receive an Anthropic invitation email — click the acceptance link and sign in with `netid@syr.edu` [[540934169]].

**Option B — University Business Credit Card:**
Go to [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com), choose "Individual," and buy credits using your SU business credit card. You're still protected by SU's enterprise agreement [[540934169]].

**Option C — Premium Seat (for high usage + higher rate limits):**
If you anticipate heavy usage, request the [Claude Premium Access Package](https://myaccess.microsoft.com/@sumailsyr.onmicrosoft.com#/access-packages/9872d51f-fd45-4c44-8d6a-e2fd2975b818). Cost is $2,400/year, pro-rated, billed to your department [[488210484]].

### If you are a Student:
Go to [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com), choose "Individual," and buy credits with your own credit card. Even when purchased this way through your SU account, you're still protected by SU's enterprise agreement [[540934169]].

> **Note for Graduate Assistants/Student Workers:** Speak with your supervisor — your department may be able to fund a premium seat or credits on your behalf [[540934169]].

---

## Phase 3: Install Claude Code & Developer Tools on Windows

### Step 3.1 — Set PowerShell Execution Policy
Open PowerShell and run [[986841103]]:
```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser
```

### Step 3.2 — Download the Install Script
Download **`Install-DevTools.ps1`** from the [Claude Code Setup page](https://answers.atlassian.syr.edu/wiki/spaces/ITSAI/pages/986841103/Claude+Code+Setup) [[986841103]].

### Step 3.3 — Remove the "Mark of the Web" (Windows security block)
Windows blocks scripts downloaded from the internet. Unblock it first [[986841103]]:

```powershell
Unblock-File -Path "$HOME\Downloads\Install-DevTools.ps1"
```
*(Or: right-click the file → Properties → check "Unblock" → OK)*

### Step 3.4 — Run the Script
```powershell
.\Install-DevTools.ps1
```
The script auto-detects your system architecture (AMD64 or ARM64) and installs all required tools [[986841103]]:

| Tool | Version | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Node.js | 24.12.0 | Portable |
| Git Portable | 2.52.0 | Includes Git Bash |
| Python Embeddable | 3.14.3 | Skipped if system Python detected |
| VS Code Portable | Latest | Skipped if already installed |
| GitHub Desktop | Latest | Git visual interface |
| PowerShell 7 | Latest | Via winget |
| Claude Code | Latest | Always installs locally |

**Default install location:** Your **OneDrive** (`%OneDrive%\Apps-SU\[arch]\<ToolName>`) for automatic sync across devices. Claude Code itself always installs locally to `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin` [[986841103]].

---

## Phase 4: Configure Claude Code to Use Your SU Account

Once installation is complete [[986841103]]:

1. Open a terminal and type: `claude`
2. Choose your preferred text display style
3. When prompted for login method, select **"Anthropic Console account"** (option 2)
4. A browser window will open — sign in with your **`netid@syr.edu`** credentials
5. If prompted, select the **Syracuse University** organization
6. Click **Authorize Claude Code** in the browser
7. Return to the terminal and **press Enter twice** to accept and trust the folder

✅ **You're configured!** Claude Code is now linked to your SU account.

---

## Phase 5: Day-to-Day Use — Key Things to Know

### Choosing the right model [[488210484]]:
| Model | Best For |
|---|---|
| **Haiku** | Quick, routine tasks (summarizing, minor edits) — uses least usage quota |
| **Sonnet** | Everyday use, general research — recommended default |
| **Opus** | Complex reasoning, large research summaries — uses most quota |

### Usage Limits [[488210484]]:
- Standard seats have usage limits that reset throughout the day
- Premium seats have higher (but not unlimited) limits
- For overflow, overage billing can be configured — email **aihelp@syr.edu**
- If limits are a concern without budget for a premium seat, consider [mentor.ai.syr.edu](http://mentor.ai.syr.edu) as an alternative (higher limits, also uses Claude models)

### Data & Security [[488210484]]:
- Code execution environments **cannot access the internet** (intentional SU security policy to protect sensitive data you bring into conversations)
- Web search in conversation is still available
- **Do not travel to Anthropic-restricted countries** and attempt to use Claude — this may result in your SU account being banned. Check [Anthropic's supported countries list](https://www.anthropic.com/supported-countries) before traveling

### Best Practices for Research [[488210484]]:
- Define your research question clearly upfront and provide all relevant data in one well-structured message
- Use Haiku for routine tasks, Sonnet/Opus for complex analysis
- If uploading files to a shared Project or Artifact, be careful about data classification of what you share

### Optional Enhancements [[986841103]]:
- **GitHub integration:** Use Git to track every change Claude Code makes to your files — commit before Claude edits, review diffs after, and easily revert if needed
- **VS Code integration:** Follow the [Claude Code VS Code Integration Guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code) for an enhanced IDE experience

---

## 🆘 Troubleshooting Quick Reference

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| Script won't run ("blocked") | Run `Unblock-File -Path "$HOME\Downloads\Install-DevTools.ps1"` [[986841103]] |
| Single-session bypass | `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\Install-DevTools.ps1` [[986841103]] |
| OneDrive not available | Run script with `-Location Local` flag [[986841103]] |
| Hitting usage limits | Email aihelp@syr.edu to discuss premium seat or overage billing [[488210484]] |
| Account banned | Submit appeal at [support.claude.com](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241253-safeguards-warnings-and-appeals) — SU cannot override Anthropic's decision [[488210484]] |
| General help | ITS Help Desk: **315-443-2677** or **help@syr.edu** [[540934169]] |

- **No OneDrive?** Add `-Location Local` to the script command [[986841103]].

results.question: What is Claude Cowork and what are the security considerations?
results.answer:
Here is a comprehensive overview of **Claude Cowork** and its security considerations at Syracuse University:

---

## What Is Claude Cowork?

Claude Cowork is a feature built into the **Claude Desktop application** that enables Claude to act as an **autonomous desktop agent**. Unlike standard Claude Chat — where you converse back and forth — Cowork can handle complex, multi-step tasks on your behalf, including reading, editing, creating, and **permanently deleting** files directly on your computer [[836698117]].

You point Cowork at a folder, describe the outcome you want, and Claude autonomously plans and executes tasks step by step. Example use cases include [[836698117]]:
- Assembling an expense report from receipt photos
- Reorganizing a messy downloads folder
- Drafting documents from source materials
- Converting files between formats

Cowork is built on the same agentic architecture as Claude Code, but designed for non-coding tasks. It launched in **January 2026** as a **research preview** and is available on macOS and Windows [[836698117]].

---

## Current Status at SU: **Disabled**

> **Cowork is currently disabled for all users in the Syracuse University Claude Enterprise organization.**

ITS made this deliberate decision after evaluating the feature's security posture and enterprise compliance fit [[836698117]].

---

## Security Considerations — Why Cowork Is Not Yet Enabled

### 1. 🚫 No Audit Log or Compliance API Coverage
This is the **most critical concern**. Anthropic has explicitly stated that Cowork activity is **not captured in Audit Logs, the Compliance API, or Data Exports** — conversation history is stored locally only. SU would have no centralized visibility into what Cowork accesses or does, making it impossible to meet institutional compliance requirements or investigate incidents [[836698117]].

### 2. 🗂️ Data Stored Locally, Not Subject to Enterprise Retention
All Cowork conversation history lives on the user's local machine, not subject to Anthropic's standard retention timeframe or SU's enterprise data governance policies. Session data could persist indefinitely — or be lost entirely if the machine is reimaged — with no organizational control [[836698117]].

### 3. 📁 Local File System Access Creates Data Exposure Risk
Cowork can read, write, and permanently delete files in any folder granted to it. If a user inadvertently points Cowork at a folder containing sensitive university data (student records, financial documents, research data, credentials), that data could be processed with no audit trail and no organizational visibility [[836698117]].

### 4. ⚠️ Prompt Injection and Agentic Risk
Because Cowork autonomously reads files, browses the web, and executes code, it is susceptible to **prompt injection attacks** — where malicious content hidden in a file or webpage tries to alter Claude's behavior. Anthropic acknowledges this risk, and there have been **documented real-world incidents** including Cowork accidentally deleting files the user did not intend to remove [[836698117]].

### 5. 🔧 No Granular Admin Controls
During research preview, Cowork is controlled by a **single organization-wide toggle** — it's all-or-nothing. There's no way to enable it for specific users, roles, or departments. Plugins are saved locally and cannot be centrally managed by admins, which doesn't align with SU's need for role-based access and centralized policy management [[836698117]].

### 6. 🔬 Research Preview Status
Cowork is still classified as a **research preview** — meaning it's in active development, safety mechanisms are still being hardened, and the product may change significantly. Enabling it at Syracuse's enterprise scale carries inherent risk given all the concerns above [[836698117]].

---

## What Can SU Users Use Instead?

While Cowork is disabled, Syracuse University users have access to robust Claude capabilities that are covered by enterprise audit and compliance controls [[836698117]]:
- **Claude Chat** (claude.ai) — Conversational AI with file upload, artifacts, projects, web search, and connectors
- **Claude Code** — Terminal-based agentic coding tool (available via premium seat purchase)
- **Claude API** — Programmatic access for building applications and automations (available via premium seat purchase)

For questions, contact the ITS Help Desk at **315-443-2677** or [help@syr.edu](mailto:help@syr.edu).

---

results.question: What is Clementine Class Search?

## Clementine: Class Search

**Clementine: Class Search** is Syracuse University's AI-powered class search tool designed to help students find the right classes faster using **natural language** — no more navigating complex catalogs or filtering through dropdowns [[895451142]].

### What Can It Do?
- **Search by topic, interest, or need** — Ask things like *"show me writing-intensive classes in the humanities"* or *"what upper-division IST classes are available this fall?"* [[895451142]]
- **Find classes meeting specific requirements** — Filter by credits, career level (undergraduate/graduate), academic term, or subject area [[895451142]]
- **Describe classes in plain language** — Get summaries and details without digging through the course catalog [[895451142]]
- **Help you plan ahead** — Explore options before your advising appointment or registration opens [[895451142]]

### Who Is It For?
Clementine is available to **all Syracuse University students**, as well as Academic Advisors and Faculty Advisors. It is especially useful during pre-registration planning, advising prep, and registration season [[895451142]].

### How to Access It
Visit **[clementine.syr.edu](https://clementine.syr.edu)**, select the Class Search Assistant, and log in with your Syracuse University credentials [[895451142]].

### Important Notes
- Clementine is **not** a replacement for the official course catalog or MySlice. Always verify enrollment details in MySlice or with your Academic Advisor [[895451142]].
- It does **not** show real-time seat availability — use MySlice for live seat counts [[895451142]].
- It is **not** an authoritative source and is subject to error; verify critical information through official university channels [[895451142]].
- It was built by the **ITS Data & AI team** and the **Registrar's Office** at Syracuse University, leveraging multiple technologies including Claude [[895451142]].

### Need Help?
Contact the ITS Service Center at 📧 help@syr.edu or 📞 315-443-2677.

results.question: What's the difference between Claude Chat, Claude Code, and the Claude API at SU?
results.answer:
Here's a comprehensive breakdown of the three Claude surfaces at Syracuse University:

---

## Claude Chat, Claude Code, and the Claude API at SU

### 🗨️ Claude Chat — Available to Everyone, Included
Claude Chat is the **default conversational interface** available to all SU students, faculty, and staff. You sign up at `getclaude.syr.edu` and access it via web, mobile, or desktop apps [[claude-at-syracuse-product-surface-map]]. It's designed for everyday tasks like writing assistance, analysis, brainstorming, research, and coding help. It is **fully covered under SU's Enterprise agreement with Anthropic**, meaning your data is not used to train Anthropic's models by default, and there is **no additional cost** [[claude-at-syracuse-product-surface-map]].

---

### 💻 Claude Code — Terminal-Based Agentic Coding, Requires Request & Payment
Claude Code is a **command-line tool** that runs in your terminal and enables agentic coding workflows — meaning Claude can take multi-step actions directly within your local development environment [[claude-at-syracuse-product-surface-map]]. It is **not included** in the standard SU Enterprise license and must be purchased separately:

- **Faculty/Staff:** Can request a Premium seat at **$2,400/year per seat** (pro-rated, funded by department), or use **pay-as-you-go credits up to $200/month** via the Claude Code API Interest and Access Request Form [[claude-at-syracuse-product-surface-map]].
- **Students:** Must purchase credits with personal funds via the Anthropic Console, though usage is still protected under SU's Enterprise agreement [[claude-at-syracuse-product-surface-map]].

Setup on Windows is supported with an automated PowerShell script that installs all required tools (Node.js, Git, Python, VS Code, and Claude Code itself) [[claude-at-syracuse-product-surface-map]].

---

### 🔌 Claude API — Programmatic Integration, Requires Request & Payment
The Claude API lets you **build applications that call Claude programmatically** — for example, embedding Claude into custom tools, workflows, or research pipelines [[claude-at-syracuse-product-surface-map]]. It is **packaged together with Claude Code** under the same access and pricing model (Premium seat or pay-as-you-go credits) [[claude-at-syracuse-product-surface-map]]. You'd use the API if you're a developer building something that integrates Claude, rather than using it interactively yourself.

---

### 📊 Quick Comparison

| Feature | Claude Chat | Claude Code | Claude API |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Who it's for** | Everyone | Developers working in terminal | Developers building apps |
| **Access** | Enabled for all SU users | Request required | Request required (same as Code) |
| **Cost** | Included in Enterprise license | Premium seat ($2,400/yr) or credits (up to $200/mo) | Same as Claude Code |
| **Interface** | Web, mobile, desktop (conversational) | Command-line terminal | Programmatic / code calls |
| **Covered by SU Enterprise agreement** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes (when purchased through SU account) | ✅ Yes |
| **Audit logging** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |

---
